readme: Adjudicated mapping from Recipe Hunter ingredient-queue terms to canonical commodity ids. THIS FILE IS THE RULING, not a hint: promote-ingredient-queue.ps1 reads only what is written here and skips anything absent. A fuzzy matcher deciding commodity identity at runtime is exactly the uncontrolled id assignment the estate guards against - a careless id splits a commodity already priced under another name.

almond flour.why: Brad 2026-08-21: new id. Verified unclaimed - flour excludes almond, so no collision.

thai chiles.why: Brad 2026-08-21: new id, dried. Both captures are McCormick Crushed Thai Style Chili Pepper, a spice jar, not fresh chiles.

cardamom pods.why: Brad 2026-08-21: new id. One store (Hy-Vee) but a real staple spice.

90/10 ground beef.why: Brad 2026-08-21: new id for 90/10 only - organic or not does not matter for the id. Placed after ground-beef-93-7 so it cannot steal from 80/20 or 93/7.

boneless beef short ribs.why: Brad 2026-08-21: keep it, filed with the meats. Verified unclaimed.

tandoori spice mix.why: Brad asked whether any store sells it: Hy-Vee does, $2.49/0.88oz Patak BBQ Tandoori Chicken Seasoning, and it is a real seasoning. 6 of 7 stores do not carry it.

Gruyere Cheese.why: Brad 2026-08-21: one new id for gruyere. Placed at index 12, ahead of apples (21), which also stops Red Apple Cheese Gruyere Cheese from matching apples.

gruyere.why: same id as Gruyere Cheese - queued twice, identical Boar's Head price.

fresh oregano.why: Brad 2026-08-21: new id, re-verify the Bakers row. dried-oregano already excludes  fresh  so there is no collision; the Bakers row (Simple Truth Organic Oregano) matches dried-oregano and is NOT fresh - it is excluded here by the dried/ground extra-excludes.

Yellow Bell Pepper.why: Brad 2026-08-21: new id. Required an exclude on bell-peppers first - its bells+peppers? include matched Yellow Bell Pepper and would have kept winning it (first-match-wins).

green bell pepper.why: Brad 2026-08-21: no new id - fold into bell-peppers and take the cheapest per lb. This also resolves the tile-integrity failure, because the cheapest per-lb row IS the $0.79 Green Bell Pepper the stored link points at.

banned.dry white wine: no wine in the catalog (canon layer; respec to broth)
banned.marsala wine: no wine in the catalog (canon layer; respec to broth)
banned.ground chicken: ground chicken is banned by the sourcer PROTEIN CLASS gate

pending_new_id.bacon bits: a shelf-stable topping, not bacon - different aisle, different basis, and reusing bacon would corrupt a live cell
pending_new_id.shaved beef steak: a specific cut/prep; the catalog names cuts individually (sirloin-steak, ribeye-steak)
pending_new_id.unsweetened ketchup: a premium variant; folding it into ketchup would make the ketchup cell look dearer than the ketchup people buy
pending_new_id.Monterey Jack Cheese: the catalog has NO block/specialty cheese ids at all (only cottage, cream, shredded, sliced, string) - this is a genuine gap, not a rename
pending_new_id.Pork Smoked Sausage: the catalog names sausages individually (italian-sausage, breakfast-sausage, smoked-turkey-sausage); pork smoked is a fourth
pending_new_id.Beef Base: beef-broth exists but a base is a concentrate paste, not a liquid - different unit basis entirely
pending_new_id.Egg Yolk: not sold as a separate retail item; the captured price is almost certainly for whole eggs, so mapping it to eggs would publish a wrong basis. Needs a human ruling on whether it is a commodity at all.
